newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Rugby Union-France beats Queensland 34-24 in Test.
newsitem.headline: Rugby Union-France beats Queensland 34-24 in Test.

text.p: France, inspired by two tries from winger Sebastien Viars, beat Queensland 34-24 on Tuesday in their final warm-up on tour before Saturday's first test against Australia.
The French, who rested the majority of their test players at Ballymore, scored five tries to two against a depleted Queensland side.
Centre Richard Dourthe also pressed his claims for test selection by scoring one try and landing three conversions and a penalty for a personal tally of 14 points.
Fullback Nicolas Brusque and hooker Raphael Ibanez scored the other tries for France, who led 22-9 at halftime.

Queensland winger Damien McInally and lock Mark Gabey scored tries for the home side, while fly-half Elton Flatley and full-back Tyron Mandrusiak kicked two penalties each. Mandrusiak added one conversion.
France, who opened their tour with easy victories against Victoria and Australian Capital Territory, will return to Ballymore on June 28 for the second and final test.

Captain Abdel Benazzi, who was rested for Tuesday's match, said:"It was very important for the French team to win this game but we know this Queensland team played without its internationals. Saturday is another game."
But he praised the performance of giant lock Olivier Brouzet, who gave a commanding performance against Queensland.
"Brouzet has a big, big future in rugby," said Benazzi. "He is a young player, has good fitness, trains hard and has plenty of ambition."
